newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent weaker Monday, based on market orders at 1017 EDT, trading sources said.
USDA today pegged planted cotton area at 14.0 million acres in 1997, compared with a forecast of 14.485 million acres in March.

The number is not likely to inspire much price activity, as the market has already absorbed the reduction. Analysts put the estimate at 13.83-14.30 million acres, and said a cut to 14.0 million acres has already been absorbed.
World cotton output, meantime, could fall to 19.05 million tons in 1997/98 from 19.319 million tons in the current season, the International Cotton Advisory Committee, said.
Global demand could rise to 19.23 million tons from 19.017 tons, while ending stocks are seen falling to 8.89 million tons from 9.085 million tons, ICAC said.
NYCE said 45 notices were issued today, bringing the total number of notices to date to 731.
Friday, benchmark December delivery closed 0.24 cent higher at 77.40 cents a lb after trading from 77.44 to 76.93 cents. The rest settled 0.20 higher to 0.05 cent weaker.
An estimated 14,000 lots changed hands on the day.
